text.p: Fred Hoiberg nailed a leaning three-pointer from the top of the key with two seconds left to take the Indiana Pacers to a 116-115 victory over the Charlotte Hornets on Friday.
After Hoiberg's desperation shot, the Hornets had a chance to win the game, but Antonio Davis batted Matt Geiger's inbounds pass away from Vlade Divac in the paint as time expired.
Reggie Miller scored 39 points for Indiana.
At the Nets, Jimmy Jackson scored 20 of his season-high 29 points in the second half to lead the New Jersey Nets to a 92-86 victory over the New York Knicks.
New York played most of the second half without star centre Patrick Ewing, who did not return after suffering a pulled muscle with 10:58 left in the third quarter.

"Any time Ewing is out of the game, you have to attack the backboard," said Jackson. "Eighty percent of their offence goes through Patrick. When Ewing went out, they lost their emotion and we fed off of that."

In Detroit, Joe Dumars scored 26 points and Lindsey Hunter added 25, and both players keyed first-half runs as the Detroit Pistons posted their most lopsided victory ever over the Los Angeles Clippers, 113-85.

Dumars, who added eight assists, closed the first half with six straight points, capping a 12-0 Pistons' run. Hunter had five straight during a first-quarter burst that turned a one-point game into a 23-13 Detroit advantage.

In Miami, Alonzo Mourning scored 23 points and grabbed 12 rebounds before he was ejected in the fourth quarter as the Miami Heat hung on for their eighth straight win, 83-79 over the reeling Cleveland Cavaliers.
The Heat jumped all over the Cavaliers, leading 34-19 after the first quarter and 57-35 at halftime as they shot 56 percent from the field (23-of-41).
P.J. Brown, who had 12 points of his 13 points in the first quarter, made one of two free throws for the final margin.
In Philadelphia, Lucious Harris scored 14 of his season-high 19 points in a pair of second-quarter runs as the Philadelphia 76ers rolled over the Boston Celtics, 113-105.
Jerry Stackhouse had 25 points, while Clarence Weatherspoon also scored 19 for Philadelphia, which is 3-0 against the Celtics this year.
Antoine Walker had a career-high 37 points for Boston.

In Washington, Chris Webber had 17 points, six rebounds, four assists and three blocked shots in the first quarter alone as the Washington Bullets exploded for a season-high 41 points in the period and coasted to a 113-86 victory over the Toronto Raptors.
Webber finished with 24 points and Juwan Howard added 22, including 14 in the second quarter, for the Bullets.
Washington is just one game behind Cleveland for the final Eastern Conference playoff berth.

In Phoenix, Kevin Johnson poured in a season-high 38 points and Rex Chapman scored the last seven points of overtime as the Phoenix Suns won their fifth straight game, outlasting the Golden State Warriors, 122-105.
Wesley Person added 28 points, including 7-of-11 from three-point range for the Suns, who jumped over the Los Angeles Clippers into seventh place in the Western Conference.

In Utah, Greg Ostertag grabbed 18 rebounds and sparked a pivotal 9-3 spurt midway through the final period with a key tip-in as the Utah Jazz established a franchise record for wins in March with a 101-96 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks.

Karl Malone scored 31 points and Jeff Hornacek added 25 for the Jazz, who are 13-1 this month. The Jazz lead Seattle by four games in the battle for homecourt advantage throughout the Western Conference playoffs.
Sherman Douglas led Milwaukee with 26 points.
In Portland, Clifford Robinson scored 26 points and Arvydas Sabonis added 18 and six rebounds as the Portland Trail Blazers routed the Vancouver Grizzlies 115-81 for their ninth-straight home win.

Robinson made 10-of-15 shots from the field, including 6-for-8 from three-point range as Portland improved to 26-10 at home. The Trail Blazers shot 55 percent (47-for-86) from the floor, making 8-of-16 shots from three-point land.

In Seattle, Hersey Hawkins and Gary Payton scored 20 points apiece and Terry Cummings had eight in the fourth quarter as the Seattle SuperSonics tied an NBA record for dominating an opponent by beating the Minnesota Timberwolves, 92-81.
The Sonics have beaten the Wolves 25 straight times, equalling the NBA mark held by the Phoenix Suns, who also defeated Minnesota 25 times in a row.
Dean Garrett scored 18 points and Kevin Garnett added 17 for Minnesota, which fell to 12-24 on the road.
